newsitem.title: SUDAN: Sudan television displays Ugandan prisoners.
newsitem.headline: Sudan television displays Ugandan prisoners.

text.p: Sudan's state television has displayed two men it said are Ugandan prisoners of war captured after a battle with Sudanese army forces in southern Sudan.
Sudan accuses Uganda of helping rebels led by the Sudan People's Liberation Army (SPAL) fighting the Khartoum Islamist government in the south and east. Uganda denies involvement.

The television late on Friday showed the two in Ugandan military uniforms. It said they were captured in Equatoria, 40 miles (64 km) southeast of southern Sudan's main town Juba, the SPLA's declared target in its bid to topple the government.
One of the men said he was a 38-year-old corporal who joined the Ugandan army in 1983. He said he came from western Uganda and was part of a battalion that entered Sudan this month.
The other, named Bawalo Kawbiri, said he belonged to Uganda's 41st infantry. He said Ugandan battalions entered Sudan through the Sudanese town of Farajok on April 2.
"The Ugandan battalions were destroyed by the Sudanese army at mile 40," Kawbiri said, adding Ugandan forces used tanks, artillery, mortars, and anti-aircraft rockets.
He said 348 Ugandan troops were killed.
The men said they were being treated well in Khartoum.

Uganda this month said its army killed 60 Sudanese soldiers and captured more than 100 inside Uganda, repulsing a joint attack by Sudan's army and Ugandan rebels. A Sudanese minister denied Sudan clashed with Ugandan forces in northern Uganda.

Forces under SPLA leader John Garang's command have stepped up their war to topple Khartoum's government. Since 1983 the SPLA has fought for independence or greater autonomy for the Christian and animist south from the Moslem and Arab north.
